scope: §7.3.10 direct/indirect equivalence as it reaches ordinary stream /Filter and /DecodeParms values under §7.4.1 and Table 5. Specifically excludes treating cross-reference streams as a generic positive case. This is a focused read/consumer/assertion audit, not certification of every stream parameter type.

source.primary: Primary direct/indirect equivalence sentence physical49/printed34 (§7.3.10); section starts48/33. §7.4.1 physical49–50; Table5 physical47; Table8 physical55–56; xrefexceptionphysical81.
source.general_rule: §7.3.10 says, except where documented to the contrary, any object value may be direct or an indirect reference and the semantics are equivalent. This includes a dictionary value such as /Filter or /DecodeParms, an array value, and array members, unless a specific clause imposes directness.
source.null_distinction: §7.3.9 is Null and dictionary-null-equivalent-to-omission. The undefined-reference-as-null rule is in §7.3.10, alongside direct/indirect equivalence. Draft attribution corrected.
source.filter_rule: §7.4.1 requires a reader to apply the named filter(s); optional parameters are specified with DecodeParms. Table 5 defines Filter as a name or array of names and DecodeParms as a dictionary or array aligned with the filter sequence. If any filter has nondefault parameters, the array has one corresponding slot per filter, with null where that stage has no parameters.
source.special_exception: §7.5.8.2 makes cross-reference stream dictionary values in Table 17 direct, including array members, and requires Filter/DecodeParms direct when that xref stream is encoded. Other xref stream entries may be indirect subject to other rules. This is a special bootstrap constraint and is not a valid counterexample to ordinary stream indirect values.
source.errata: EC3 #246 expands the cross-reference stream directness rule to all Table 5 entries, arrays and dictionary key values, and prohibits /F; #720 updates the list of entries that may be indirect. These are xref-stream-specific exceptions, not a change to ordinary stream semantics. No amendment found to §7.3.10's generic equivalence sentence or §7.4.1's filter/parameter assignment in this selected review.

features.requirement: For a normal stream, a Filter name or array may be indirect under §7.3.10. In a filter array, a name element may itself be an indirect object. The reader must still apply the resulting chain in order.
features.implementation: crates/pdf-syntax/src/document/objects.rs::get_key resolves the stream dictionary's Filter value. crates/pdf-syntax/src/document/decoding.rs::filter_chain then resolves each array element before interpreting it as a name.
features.existing_assertions: crates/pdf-syntax/tests/filters.rs::a_filter_array_is_a_pipeline_is direct-only. It proves ordering with ASCII85 around Flate and expected text bytes. Inspected stream-filter tests contain no direct-versus-indirect /Filter comparison; there is no asserted indirect Filter name or indirect filter-array/member consumer fixture.
features.draft: drafts/indirect_filter_parameters_spec_audit.rs::indirect_filter_name_and_decodeparms_dictionary_match_direct_values compares a direct /FlateDecode control to /Filter 5 0 R where object 5 is the Name /FlateDecode. It asserts known decoded samples and exact xref/no recovery.
features.verdict: Implementation follows the generic rule; the specific ordinary-stream indirect Filter shape lacks an inspected discriminating assertion. Draft is a positive coverage addition, not a confirmed behavior failure.

features.requirement: An ordinary stream's DecodeParms dictionary or array, and a dictionary occupying one filter's array slot, may be indirect. Each array slot still belongs to its corresponding filter; null denotes no parameter dictionary for that stage.
features.implementation: crates/pdf-syntax/src/document/decoding.rs::decode_parms resolves the whole DecodeParms value through get_key and resolves an array member before requiring a dictionary. Filter dispatch passes that per-stage dictionary to filter::stage/decode_with_parms. The predictor consumer is part of FlateDecode/LZWDecode/CCITTFaxDecode implementation paths.
features.existing_assertions: filters.rs::each_stage_takes_its_own_entry_of_a_decodeparms_array uses [null, direct predictor dict] for ASCII85+Flate and checks exact unpredicted row bytes; lzw_full_table_audit.rs tests direct EarlyChange dictionaries and absent/default behavior; CCITT tests use direct parameters and image assertions. jbig2_filter_chain_audit.rs has an indirect /JBIG2Globals object inside a direct DecodeParms dictionary, which does not test an indirect DecodeParms value or dictionary itself.
features.draft: drafts/indirect_filter_parameters_spec_audit.rs::indirect_filter_and_decodeparms_arrays_resolve_each_stage_value compares a direct two-stage filter/parameter array with indirect /Filter and /DecodeParms arrays, indirect filter names, and an indirect predictor dictionary in the Flate slot. Its raw PNG predictor rows have literal expected sample bytes; no decoder is used to calculate the expected output.
features.verdict: The inspected consumers resolve each reference at the appropriate level. Direct-form tests are strong for parameter semantics but do not demonstrate indirect representations. Draft adds valid indirect positive controls; no current failure is established.

features.requirement: Cross-reference streams are exceptional: §7.5.8.2 Table 17 values are direct, including array entries; Filter and DecodeParms must be direct if encoded; #246 broadens the rule to all Table 5 entries and prohibits /F.
features.implementation: crates/pdf-syntax/src/xref.rs::decode_direct intentionally inspects the xref stream dictionary without Document::get_key or reference resolution and only accepts directly stated Name/Array filter forms and directly stated parameter dictionaries.
features.assertions: Existing xref stream tests use direct dictionary values. They are not reused as evidence for general ordinary-stream indirection. The directness condition is principally a producer rule; this audit does not infer a required reader rejection policy for invalid xref streams.
features.verdict: The implementation has a deliberate bootstrap boundary consistent with the special source rule; kept out of the ordinary stream positive fixtures.

features.requirement: Generic §7.3.10 equivalence applies to Table8 integer values; no ordinary-stream direct-only exception found.
features.implementation: decode_parms resolves outerdictionary but leaves numeric values as references; filter.rs reads Predictor/Columns using raw Object::as_integer and substitutes defaults.
features.parent_execution: Two new parent testsFAIL after literal directcontrolsPASS. IndirectPredictor15 returns still-predicted eightbytes; indirectColumns3 refuses decoding. Outerrepresentationtwo testsPASS.
features.verdict: B54 confirmed; numericvalues are a distinct layer omitted from initial agent draft.
features.limits: Only Predictor andColumns failure witnessed. No all-codec or all-key failure claim.

drafts: drafts/indirect_filter_parameters_spec_audit.rs: indirect single Filter/DecodeParms dictionary pair; indirect filter and DecodeParms arrays with indirect members and an independent PNG predictor byte oracle. Drafts are unexecuted and parent-owned for integration/run.
limits: The draft uses the ordinary Flate/ASCII85 content-stream path; no claim is made about every codec-specific DecodeParms key or every reference chain length.
No malformed-only rejection requirement is inferred from §7.3.9's undefined-reference-as-null rule.
No Cargo command or production/ledger mutation was performed.
